answer: Each epoch, every identity must draw one unique live job from the public lagoon of open tasks and perform it at the wharf checkpoint, a timed public dock where three randomly chosen unrelated peers watch the session as it happens. The finished work is then presented at the summit review, where the same witnesses sign it. A recording cannot substitute for live presence, and each job, panel, and session is unique — so one operator running a thousand clones must stage a thousand distinct live jobs under a thousand random panels, with no way to pool or replay a single performance.
